steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added to the file.
successCriteria: The code includes a valid import statement that imports both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement needs some adjustment. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using the correct syntax.

steps.title: Import createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'
steps.hint: Use a named import from the RTK Query package to get these utilities.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing RTK Query utilities
import { createApi, fetchBaseQuery } from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the RTK Query utilities imported and ready to create an API service.
successCriteria: The import statement should bring in createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported createApi and fetchBaseQuery. These are the core utilities for building RTK Query APIs with automatic request deduplication.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns null for now. Use TypeScript syntax.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named App that returns null. Remember to specify the return type as JSX.Element.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a functional component named App that returns null.
successCriteria: The component must be named App, be a function or arrow function, and return null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the App component structure. This gives us a starting point to build our request deduplication example.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named App that returns null. Check the syntax and return type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. You need to create a functional component named App that returns null.

steps.title: Create an API service using createApi
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'api' using the imported createApi function with an empty configuration object.
steps.hint: Use the createApi function you imported earlier. Call it with an empty object {} and assign the result to a constant named api.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of creating an API service with createApi
const api = createApi({});
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a constant named 'api' created with createApi({}).
successCriteria: It uses the imported createApi function
It's called with an empty object {}
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an API service instance using createApi. This is the foundation for setting up RTK Query endpoints.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you name the constant 'api'? Are you using the imported createApi function? Is it called with an empty object {}?
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review: You need to create a constant named 'api' using createApi({}). Make sure you're using the createApi function imported earlier.

steps.title: Define baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery
steps.instruction: Inside the createApi configuration object, add a baseQuery property that uses fetchBaseQuery with a baseUrl set to 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com'.
steps.hint: Add the baseQuery property to the object passed to createApi. Use fetchBaseQuery with a baseUrl option.
steps.expectedOutcome: The API service configuration now includes a baseQuery property that defines the base URL for all API requests.
successCriteria: The code must include a baseQuery property inside the createApi configuration object, using fetchBaseQuery with a baseUrl option set to 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully configured the base query for your API service. This sets the foundation URL for all requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the baseQuery configuration needs adjustment. Make sure you're using fetchBaseQuery with a baseUrl option set to 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com' inside the createApi object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The baseQuery configuration is missing or incorrect. You need to add a baseQuery property to the createApi configuration object that uses fetchBaseQuery with a baseUrl.

steps.title: Define endpoints with a single query endpoint
steps.instruction: Add an 'endpoints' property to your API service configuration object. Inside it, define a single query endpoint named 'getPosts' that fetches data from the '/posts' URL path.
steps.hint: The 'endpoints' property should be an object where each key is an endpoint name. For a query endpoint, use a function that returns an object with a 'query' property specifying the URL path.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your API service should now have an 'endpoints' property with a 'getPosts' query endpoint that will fetch from '/posts' when called.
successCriteria: The code should include an 'endpoints' property in the createApi configuration object, containing a 'getPosts' query endpoint with a 'query' property set to '/posts'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the endpoints property with a getPosts query endpoint. This endpoint will be used to demonstrate request deduplication in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there might be a small issue. Make sure you've added the 'endpoints' property correctly and defined a 'getPosts' query endpoint that fetches from '/posts'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to add an 'endpoints' property to the createApi configuration object, with a single query endpoint named 'getPosts' that fetches from '/posts'.

steps.title: Initialize state for tracking request count
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named requestCount, initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState<number>(0) and destructure the returned array into requestCount and its setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of creating a numeric state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState<number>(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a requestCount state variable available to track how many times requests are made.
successCriteria: The code must include a useState call with type parameter <number> and initial value 0, destructured into requestCount and its setter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the requestCount state variable. This will allow us to monitor request frequency.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using useState<number>(0) and destructuring into [requestCount, setRequestCount].
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on creating the state variable. Use useState<number>(0) inside the App component to create requestCount.

steps.title: Define handler to trigger multiple requests
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, create a function called handleMultipleRequests that will be used to demonstrate request deduplication. This function should call the getPosts endpoint multiple times and update the requestCount state to track how many times it's been called.
steps.hint: Define an async function that uses the api.endpoints.getPosts.initiate() method multiple times and increments the requestCount state variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleMultipleRequests function is defined that will trigger multiple API requests and update the request counter.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleMultipleRequests, call api.endpoints.getPosts.initiate() at least twice, and update the requestCount state using setRequestCount.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handler function that will demonstrate request deduplication by making multiple API calls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function calls the API endpoint multiple times and properly updates the requestCount state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't seem to be defined correctly. Remember to create an async function named handleMultipleRequests that calls api.endpoints.getPosts.initiate() multiple times and updates the requestCount state.

steps.title: Add a container div to the component return
steps.instruction: Wrap the existing JSX content inside the App component's return statement with a div element that has className 'app'.
steps.hint: Add a <div className="app"> element as the outermost container, then place the existing <h1> inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component's JSX is now wrapped in a div with className 'app'.
successCriteria: The return statement must contain a div element with className 'app' that wraps the existing h1 element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a container div with className 'app' to structure your UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've wrapped the h1 element inside a div with className 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container div with className 'app' is missing or not properly wrapping the content.

steps.title: Add a heading to explain request deduplication
steps.instruction: Add an h2 element with explanatory text about request deduplication inside the container div, below the existing h1 element.
steps.hint: Add a new <h2> element with text that explains what request deduplication does. Place it after the existing <h1> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will now have an explanatory heading below the main title, providing context about request deduplication.
successCriteria: The code should contain an h2 element with explanatory text about request deduplication, placed inside the container div after the h1 element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added an explanatory heading that will help users understand the purpose of this example.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added an h2 element with explanatory text about request deduplication, placed after the existing h1 element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading wasn't added correctly. You need to add an h2 element with text explaining request deduplication, placed inside the container div after the h1 element.

steps.title: Display the request count state
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current requestCount value. The paragraph should show the text 'Request count: ' followed by the requestCount value.
steps.hint:
Add a

tag inside the existing

after the

. Use curly braces {} to embed the requestCount variable in the JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current requestCount value (which is currently 0) in a paragraph below the heading.
successCriteria: The paragraph element should be added inside the existing <div> after the <h1> and should display the text 'Request count: ' followed by the requestCount value using JSX interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added a paragraph that displays the current requestCount value. This demonstrates how state updates are reflected in the UI in real-time.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the paragraph doesn't fully meet the requirements. Make sure you're displaying the text 'Request count: ' followed by the actual requestCount value using curly braces {}.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element is missing or doesn't display the requestCount value correctly. Remember to add a

steps.title: Add the trigger button and wire its onClick
steps.instruction: Inside the App component's return statement, add a button element with the text 'Trigger Multiple Requests' and wire its onClick event to the handleMultipleRequests function.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element inside the container div, after the heading and paragraph. Set its onClick prop to handleMultipleRequests.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will now include a button that, when clicked, will trigger the handleMultipleRequests function (which will be defined in the next step).
successCriteria: The button element must be present inside the container div, have the text 'Trigger Multiple Requests', and its onClick prop must be set to handleMultipleRequests.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the trigger button and wired it to the handler function. The button is now ready to demonstrate request deduplication when the handler is implemented.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it's missing either the correct text or the onClick handler. Make sure the button says 'Trigger Multiple Requests' and has onClick={handleMultipleRequests}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or incorrectly implemented. Add a <button> element with the text 'Trigger Multiple Requests' and wire its onClick to handleMultipleRequests.

steps.title: Export the App component
steps.instruction: Export the App component as the default export so it can be imported in other files.
steps.hint: Use the 'export default' syntax followed by the component name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Export the component as default
export default App;
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is exported as the default export, making it available for import elsewhere.
successCriteria: The code includes 'export default App;' (or equivalent) after the component definition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the App component as the default export. This makes it available for use in other files, completing the component setup.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the export might be incomplete. Ensure you use 'export default App;' (or equivalent) to export the component as the default.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not exported as default. Add 'export default App;' (or equivalent) to make the component available for import.
